# Specific Aims

Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a very important and timely problem with many applications in modern medicine. In recent years, artificial intelligence has achieved remarkable success across a wide range of domains, and it has the potential to revolutionize nephrology. In this proposal, we will explore whether routinely collected laboratory trends might possibly help identify patients at risk of rapid eGFR decline.

Our long-term goal is to make kidney-function decline predictable early enough to change care. The objective of this application is to develop and validate a risk model for rapid eGFR decline. Our central hypothesis is that machine learning could perhaps be useful for this problem.

**Aim 1:** Apply gradient-boosted trees to the EHR dataset.

**Aim 2:** Extend the model from Aim 1 to a second health system.

**Aim 3:** If Aims 1 and 2 succeed, run a pilot clinical decision-support study.

Our team is uniquely positioned to carry out this groundbreaking work. This project will have a large impact on the field and will foster the next generation of nephrology data scientists.
